en: Now begins the Chapter on the Bolt (Argalādhyāya), Chapter 31.
O Sage, I desire now to hear about that *yārgalā* which was described by you as bestowing auspiciousness, along with its characteristics and its fruit. (1)
O Maitreya, that which is called the "bolt" (sārgalā), by which the results of the planets become firm and stable, shall now be described by me. (2)
And when a planet is in the fourth or the eleventh house, its *argalā* is to be known [there].
The planets that obstruct it are, in order, those situated in the tenth, the twelfth, and the third houses. (3)
Those who are weak or inferior in number are not considered obstructors;
however, O Maitreya, in the third [period], those who are diseased and sinful are the obstructors.
Even there, O best of the twice-born, the *argalā* (obstacle) should be understood as being reversed;
nevertheless, the wise know that the results of the planetary houses are obstructed by the *argalā*.
The fifth is the position of the bolt (argalā), and the ninth is its adversary;
that [ninth] arises from the planet Tamas, O twice-born one, and is known through its reversal.
That which has one *graha* is the lowest; it is remembered as the middling when it has two *grahas*;
and that which arises with more than two is declared by the sages to be the best, known as *argalā*.
The *argalā* is to be understood as being of two kinds, both according to the zodiacal sign (*rāśi*) and according to the planet (*graha*):
that which is unobstructed yields good results, while that which is obstructed is fruitless. (8)
O best of the twice-born, when a planet is situated in a particular zodiacal sign, its results should be known without doubt at the time of that sign's period (pākāntara).
O Brahmin, how should one contemplate the *argalā* (bolt) and the *pratibandha* (obstruction) in relation to the fourth feet, and between the second and third feet? This is my opinion.
When the Nirābhāsā-argalā occurs in the ascendant or in the seventh house,
then the person born will be highly renowned and endowed with great fortune.
If a malefic or even a benefic planet should occupy a favorable *ārgala*, the ascendant aspected by that planet is rendered strong. (12)
O Brahmin, in the third [house], there is wealth secured by bolts, as well as abundance of riches and grain; the wise have declared that happiness for siblings and others resides therein.
In the fourth [house], he is endowed with houses, livestock, bonds, and kinsmen;
in the fifth, the man is possessed of sons, grandsons, and so forth, and is intelligent.
In the sixth house there is fear of enemies; in the seventh, there is much happiness regarding wealth and wife;
in the eighth, suffering arises; and in the ninth, there shall be the dawn of good fortune. (15)
In the tenth house, there is honor from the king; in the eleventh house, one is endowed with gains; and in the twelfth house, O Brahmin, an excess of expenditure occurs.
When there is an auspicious planetary bolt (śubhagrahārgalā), there will be manifold happiness;
when there is a malefic bolt (pāpārgalā), it is middling; and even when there is a mixed bolt (miśrārgalā), it is excellent.
O best of the twice-born, when the ascendant, the fifth house, and the ninth house are secured by argalas, one who is born becomes a king and fortunate; there is no doubt in this matter.
Now begins the chapter on the agents of action (kāraka). || 32 ||
Now I shall fully describe the planets, which are the causal agents beginning with the self (the soul), numbering eight—either from the Sun to Śani (Saturn) or including Rāhu. || 1 ||
If there are two planets occupying the same degrees, one should then consider them as Rāhu and Anta;
thus, some declare that there are seven Karakas, while others say eight. || 2 ||
Among the planets beginning with the Sun, the self (the ascendant) is indeed the planet that has the greatest degrees;
in the case of equality of degrees, it is the one with more minutes; and in the case of equality of those as well, it is the one with more seconds. (3)
In the case of Mercury, if it exceeds the degrees of its sign, it is not considered a *grāhya* (receivable) *kāraka*;
rather, one exceeding the degrees (*aṃśa*) is a *kāraka*, while one with fewer degrees is an *antya-kāraka* (final *kāraka*). || 4 ||
The middle portion shall be the middle planet, and that indeed is the secondary planet (upakheṭa). Because Rāhu moves in retrograde, its degrees should be subtracted from thirty (khavahni). || 5 ||
Those situated progressively lower and lower in the sequence of divisions are called the "moving" (cara) agents (kārakas).
Among them, O twice-born one, the agent called the "Self" (ātman) is said to be the primary one.
O best of the twice-born, that very lord of the Jātaka should be understood as being like the king who is renowned on earth as the protector of men. (7)
He is the overseer of all affairs, as well as the one who binds and the one who releases.
Just as by the king's command the Brahmins, sons, ministers,
and other people are capable of performing the affairs of the world, so too are all other causal factors.
O twice-born one, in this world, all things become fruit-bearing only when they are favorable to oneself; just as all ministers and others are [ineffective] when the king is hostile.
Indeed, when the Atmakaraka is cruel, other planets are not capable of bestowing auspiciousness upon men for the performance of their actions. || 11 ||
O twice-born one, just as all ministers and others do not perform any evil when the king is well-disposed,
so too others do not bestow evil upon him.
The minister as a functional agent possesses fewer degrees than the self, the agent, and the portion;
the brother has fewer degrees than that, and the one designated as the mother has even fewer than him. (13)
The father has a portion less than that; therefore, he who produces a son has a smaller share.
A kinsman has a portion less than the son, and indeed, one who is a relative has a portion less than the kinsman. (14)
O best of the twice-born, he should be known as a *dārakāraka* (one who causes the birth of a son) when he is free from doubt;
these have been declared by the Brahmins of old to be the so-called *carākaras*. 15.
Others say that it is the mother-maker alone who is the child-maker;
if two planets of equal strength should arise for anyone at their birth. (16)
O best of the twice-born, the elision of the very first letter [of the name] should be understood in this manner;
the auspicious or inauspicious fruit of that [name] should be known by virtue of its stable letter. || 17 ||
Now I shall fully describe the hand-holds known as "stable" (sthira).
That which is strong between the Sun and Venus is to be known as the Pitṛ-kāraka (the paternal hand-hold). || 18 ||
The planet possessing strength between the Moon and the Sun is called the maternal indicator (mātṛkāraka).
From Mars, [the planets indicate] a sister, a younger brother-in-law, and also a mother. (19)
From Mercury come kinsmen of the mother’s caste and maternal uncles;
from Venus comes the preceptor; from Jupiter the paternal grandfather; and from Saturn the father’s son.
The wife of the Brahmin’s pupil, one's parents, one's parents-in-law, and maternal grandfathers and so forth—these are to be cared for, and they are the ones who provide stability. (21)
Now, O twice-born one, I shall describe the agents (kārakas) according to the planets and houses:
the father is from the Sun in the second house, O dear one, and the mother is in the fourth from the Moon.
From Mars, in the third house, is a brother; from Mercury, in the sixth, is a maternal uncle;
from Jupiter, in the fifth, is a son; and from Venus, in the seventh, is a wife.
One should consider the death of the father and other relatives resulting from the bite of a Mandā snake;
having thus deliberated upon everything, the wise man should declare each respective result. (24)
Now, O twice-born one, I shall explain in this context the planets that cause [various] yogas for one born at birth, according to their mixed positions.

Planets situated mutually in angles (kendras) in one's own sign, in their exaltation, or in the sign of a friend are all considered *kārakas* (agents of action); among them, however, the one occupying the tenth house is especially so. || 26 ||
O twice-born one, just as planets situated in their own signs or exaltations in the ascendant, the fourth,
or the seventh house are called *kārakas*, they become so especially when situated in the tenth house.

If one planet is situated in its own house, a friendly sign, or its exaltation, and another planet is situated in a quadrant from it, they are mutual friends; endowed with such qualities, that [second] planet is also called a *kāraka*.
O Brahmin, even one born into a low lineage, provided there is a favorable planetary factor present, becomes honored by kings, wealthy, and endowed with happiness. (29)
One born into a royal lineage certainly becomes a king;
thus, one should declare the fruit for the doers according to their family lineage. (30)
Now I shall fully explain the specific characteristics of the agents of manifestation;
one should know that the birth-ascendant of a person is the agent of the self (ātmakāraka). || 31 ||
One should understand the house of wealth (the second house) as indeed the maker of wives;
it belongs to the elder brother in the eleventh house, but to the younger brother in the third house. (32)
One should recognize the son from the fifth house and the wife from the seventh house;
whichever planet is situated in the house of the son, that too is called a Kāraka.
The Sun, Jupiter, Mars, the Moon, Jupiter, Mars, Venus, Saturn, Jupiter, Mercury, Jupiter, and Saturn are the planets that cause existence (bhava). || 34 ||
Furthermore, the houses beginning with the body (the first house) are to be established as the *bhāvas*; their auspiciousness or inauspiciousness [is determined by the planets therein].
The second, third, eighth, sixth, second, and twelfth houses are designated as the houses of gain, siblings, death, enemies, wealth, and expenditure, respectively. (35)
O best of the twice-born, these states have been fully described as being called "cruel.
Through the conjunction of these, the loss of whatever state [is present] occurs. (36)
O best of the twice-born, the houses known as the quadrants (kendras) and those called the angles (koṇas) are auspicious;
by their mere conjunction, even that which is inauspicious becomes auspicious. (37)
Now begins the thirty-third chapter: On the Results of the Portion of the Karakas.
Now, O twice-born one, I shall duly declare the results of the portions of the signs, beginning with Aries, when they are in their own divisions, as spoken by Brahmā. (1)

O Brahmin, when the Moon is in the sign of Aries and the Sun is the significator of the house, there will always be mice and cats in the home causing fear, especially if they are joined with malefic planets.
When its own Vṛṣa divisional portion is occupied, four-footed animals grant happiness;
when that [planet] is in the Mithuna divisional portion, there arises the occurrence of diseases such as itching and the like.
In the Cancer portion, there is fear of water; in the Leo portion, danger from wild beasts;
in the Virgo portion, itching and corpulence, as well as fear from sparks of fire.
If Libra is the portion, one is born as a merchant, skillful in the manufacture of garments and the like;
if Scorpio is the portion, there is fear of snakes and affliction from the mother's breast.
In the Dhanuṣa division, there is a fall from a height or even from a vehicle;
likewise, in the Maraka division, death occurs due to creatures born of water or by aerial predators.
Through conch shells, pearls, corals, and the like, certain gain is obtained;
and one born in the portion of Kumbha becomes a maker of tanks and similar works.
O best of the twice-born, one born when the significator is in the portion of Pisces attains liberation;
there is no inauspiciousness when it is aspected by benefics, nor is there auspiciousness when it is aspected by malefics.
O Brahmin, if the Karakamsa is auspicious, the Lagnamsa contains a benefic planet, and it is aspected by a benefic, the person born will certainly become a king. || 9 ||

If auspicious planets, free from malefics, occupy a quadrant or a trine from their own Navāṃśa, the native is endowed with wealth and learning; if they are mixed, one should declare the results to be mixed.
O best of Brahmins, when the Moon is in its exaltation, its own sign, or a benefic sign during its period,
and is free from the aspect of malefic planets, one should predict liberation for that person at the end.
If the Karaka is situated in a division (varga) of the Moon, Mars, or Venus, the native is an adulterer;
if it is otherwise, the wise should understand all results to be the opposite. 12.
O twice-born one, if the Sun is in the Karaka portion, the person born will be devoted to royal service;
if it is the Full Moon, he will be an enjoyer and learned, especially if it is aspected by Venus. || 13 ||
If Mars is endowed with strength in its own division, the person born will be a lover of weapons;
he may also become a fire-worker or a practitioner of alchemy. (14)
When Mercury is endowed with strength and situated in its own division, one becomes skilled in the arts and crafts, proficient in trade, and possessed of intelligence and learning. || 15 ||
When Jupiter is in its own sign, a man becomes a performer of good deeds, devoted to knowledge, and a knower of the Vedas;
when Venus is there, he becomes a master of a hundred senses, lustful, and a servant of the king.
If Saturn is situated in its own division, the person born performs actions appropriate to his own family;
and if Rāhu is there, he is born as a thief, an archer, or a maker of iron implements.
Or else, O Brahmin, he is born as a physician of poisons; there is no doubt in this matter.
Under Ketu, one becomes a consumer of elephants and other such things, and is born as a thief.
When the Sun and Rāhu are in their own divisions, fear arises from serpents;
if they are aspected by benefics, there is no fear at all, but if aspected by malefics, death may occur. || 19 ||
When the Karakāṃśa is conjoined with the six auspicious planets and aspected by Mars, and is further joined by the Sun and Rāhu, one becomes a physician for poisons.
Those who do not look into the houses of others are like those who burn their own homes; however, when that [house] is observed by a wise man, the burner of fire does not arise at all.
O best of Brahmins, if the malefic planet is aspected by Jupiter, it causes the burning of a nearby house;
however, if it is aspected by Venus, no burning of the house occurs.
If Gulika is conjoined with its own Navamsha and aspected by a full Moon, one becomes a thief who has stolen wealth, or he may become a thief himself. || 23 ||
If Gulika is aspected by Mars in the eighth house, there is either misfortune or he is killed by poison;
if aspected by Mercury, he becomes a great progenitor—of this there is no doubt. (24)
O best of the twice-born, if the seventh house or the Karaka for that house is aspected by a malefic,
the person born will suffer from ear disease or undergo the cutting off of an ear.
If that [ascendant] is aspected by the son of Bhṛgu (Venus), the person becomes initiated;
if it is aspected by Mercury and Saturn, the man certainly becomes devoid of virility. (26)
If that [sign] is aspected by Mercury and Venus, a son of a female slave is born, or else a son of a remarried woman is born; there is no doubt in this matter. || 27 ||
If he is seen by Saturn alone, the person born will be an ascetic, or perhaps a servant;
if he is seen by Saturn alone, the one born will wear the garb of a renunciant.
If that [sign] is aspected by the Sun and Venus, the person will become a servant of the king.
Thus, O twice-born one, the results of the portions of the Karakas have been declared in brief. (29)

If Venus and Mars are in their own divisions or in the division of another's wife (pāradārika), one should know from the aspectual conjunction of those two that this result will persist until death. (30)

If Ketu is in the second house from the Karakamsha, there would be an obstruction to that [wealth]; if Jupiter is there, it is specifically for women; and if Rahu is there, there would be a cessation of wealth. || 31 ||
If a malefic planet is situated in the third house from its own Navamsha, the person born will be brave and powerful;
if a benefic planet is there, he will be timid—of this there is no doubt. (32)
If the fourth house from its own sign is conjoined with or aspected by the Moon and Venus,
or if a planet is situated there in its exaltation, the native will possess palaces.
If that [ascendant] is joined by Saturn and Rāhu, the house for the newborn is made of stone;
if by Mars and Ketu, it is made of bricks; and if by Jupiter, it is a wooden house.
O twice-born one, it has been declared by Ravi that for one born under Tārṇa, there is the acquisition of a house;
however, if the Moon is in an unobstructed region, a wife and progeny are produced.
In the fifth house, if it is aspected by both Mars and Rāhu, there arises the possibility of consumption (kṣayaroga); if aspected by the Lord of Night (the Moon), it certainly comes to pass.
If Mars aspects [the Moon], the person born will suffer from diseases such as boils;
if Ketu aspects it, O twice-born one, there will be dysentery or a water-related disease.
If there is a Sarāhu-gulikā there, fear arises from hunger and poison;
if it is Budha, a Paramahaṃsa or a staff-bearer is born. (38)
When the Sun is [the ruler], one becomes a bearer of the sword; when Mars, one should be a wielder of the spear;
when Saturn, he is to be known as a bowman; and when Rāhu, he possesses iron engines.
O twice-born one, when Ketu is in the ascendant, a man is born as a maker of water-clocks;
but when Venus is there, a person is born as a poet, eloquent, and a knower of poetry.

The author [states that] this [planet] is [situated] in its own division or in the fifth from it by means of the Moon and Jupiter; it is slightly less than that by Venus, and even smaller than that by Mercury. (41)
Even though he was a teacher, an omniscient author of treatises, a knower of the Vedas and Vedānta, and a master of grammar and eloquence, he was not [regarded as such] by the Guru alone. (42)
He is a Naiyāyika through Mars, a Mīmāṃsaka through Mercury, a fool in assemblies through Saturn, and one who knows song through the Sun. (43)
By the moon [planet] he becomes a knower of Sāṃkhya and Yoga, and a singer who knows the science of literature;
by Ketu he becomes a knower of mathematics, and likewise by Rāhu as well. (44)
O twice-born one, the success of the tradition comes from the connection with the guru;
some indeed say that the fruit arises from one's own portion as the second [cause]. (45)
If a malefic planet is situated in the sixth house from its own sign, a person is born as a cultivator;
if it is a benefic planet, he is lazy—this result is also recorded for the third house.
If Jupiter is in the seventh house for one, his wife is exceedingly beautiful;
if Venus is there, she is passionate, and if Mercury, she is skilled in the arts.

If [the Moon] is in the Sun's own sign (Leo), she is hidden from her family; if in Saturn's, she is advanced in age; if in Rāhu's, she is known as an ascetic woman, or afflicted by disease, or a widow. || 48 ||
If the eighth house is joined with its own lord, one is said to have a long life from the perspective of its own division (svāṃśa).
If it is joined with or aspected by malefics, there is short life; if joined with or aspected by mixed [planets], there is middling life. (49)
If the ninth house from the Karakamsha is conjoined with or aspected by a benefic planet,
the man is truthful, devoted to his guru, and dedicated to his own dharma.
If the ninth house from its own sign is conjoined with or aspected by malefic planets,
one is devoted to one's own duty in youth, but becomes a speaker of falsehood in old age.
If Saturn and Rāhu are conjoined with or aspect the Karakāṃśa in the ninth house,
the man will be a traitor to his guru and averse to the sacred scriptures.
If the ninth house from the Karakamsha is conjoined with or aspected by Jupiter and the Sun,
even then one will be a traitor to his guru and will not respect the words of his guru.
If the ninth house from the Karakāṃśa is conjoined with or aspected by Venus and Mars,
and there is a configuration such as the Ṣaḍvarga yoga, death resulting from adultery occurs.
O twice-born one, if the ninth house from the Karakamsha is conjoined with or aspected by Mercury and the Moon, the boy will certainly become a slave through union with another's wife. 55.
If the ninth house is conjoined with or aspected by Jupiter alone,
the one born will be a lover of women and will indeed become a seeker of sensual pleasures.
If the tenth house from the Karakamsha is conjoined with or aspected by a benefic planet, the child will possess stable wealth, be profound, and endowed with strength and intelligence. 57.
If, in the tenth house from the Kārakāṃśa, there is a malefic planet joined with or aspecting it, loss occurs in one's occupation, and the native is deprived of paternal happiness. (58)
In the tenth house, if it is conjoined with or aspected by Mercury and Venus from the Kārakāṃśa,
the man will have great gain in his occupation and will be a performer of great deeds.
O Brahmin, if the tenth house from the Karakamsha is conjoined with or aspected by the Sun and the Moon, and is also aspected by or conjoined with Jupiter, the native shall possess royal power.
If the eleventh house from its own sign is conjoined with or aspected by benefic planets,
the native will possess happiness from brothers and bring success in all undertakings.
But if the eleventh house is associated with a malefic, the man becomes famous and valorous, though he leads others onto evil paths; of this there is no doubt.
If a benefic planet is situated in the twelfth house from the Karakamsha, there will be virtuous expenditure;
if a malefic is there, one should know there is unvirtuous expenditure; and in the absence of any planet, the result is auspicious.
If a benefic planet is situated in the twelfth house from the Karakamsha and is in its own sign or exaltation, that person attains a good state and reaches an auspicious world. || 64 ||
If Ketu is in the twelfth house from the Karakamsha and is joined with or aspected by a benefic planet, then liberation occurs and one attains the state of Sāyujya. || 65 ||
If Ketu is situated in the twelfth house from the Karakāṃśa in Aries or Sagittarius,
and is aspected by a benefic planet, one shall attain the state of union (Sāyujya).
When Ketu is situated solely in the twelfth house, whether conjoined with or aspected by malefic planets,
liberation does not then occur, nor does one behold the auspicious world.
O best of the twice-born, when Ketu is conjoined with the Sun and situated in the twelfth house from the Karakāṃśa,
devotion to Śiva will undoubtedly arise.
When Ketu is conjoined with the Moon and situated in the twelfth house from the Karakamsha,
that man will have devotion to Gauri and becomes a follower of the Shakta path.
When Ketu is conjoined with Venus and situated in the twelfth house from the Karakamsha, devotion to Lakshmi arises; such a person born is indeed prosperous. || 70 ||
If Ketu is conjoined with Mars, the man will be a devotee of Skanda; if with Mercury and Saturn, he will be a Vaiṣṇava; and if with Jupiter, he will possess devotion to Śiva.
Rāhu serves the dark and difficult goddess Kṣudradevatā;
his devotion is likewise directed toward Skanda or Heramba, or perhaps toward Śikhin alone. (72)
When Saturn is in the twelfth house from the Karakamsha and situated in a malefic sign, even then there is no doubt that he has devotion to a minor deity. || 73 ||
Even if Saturn or Venus is in a malefic sign, one is then a servant of the lowly;
one should declare the results in this same manner for the sixth and seventh houses from the Amatyakaraka.
O twice-born one, when two malefic planets are situated in a trine from the Karakamsha, a man is born who is a knower of mantra and tantra; of this there is no doubt. (75)
If it is gazed upon there by malefic planets, one born therein will be a persecutor;
if it is gazed upon by benefic planets, that man will be a benefactor. || 76 ||
If the Moon is aspected by Venus in its own division, the man will be an alchemist;
and if it is aspected by Mercury, he will be a good physician who cures all diseases.
If the Moon is aspected by Venus in the fourth house, the man will suffer from leprosy and vitiligo;
if aspected by Mars, he will be afflicted with a great disease and suffering from hemorrhagic fever (raktapitta). || 78 ||
If the Moon is in Ketu-dṛṣṭi (aspected by Ketu) and in the fourth or fifth house, one is born with blue leprosy, provided that Rāhu and Mars are situated there on the day [of birth]. (79)
If Mars is situated alone in the fourth or the fifth house from its own division (svāṃśa) and is aspected by the Moon, consumption (kṣayaroga) will certainly afflict him.
When Ketu is situated there, he will undoubtedly suffer from diseases such as abdominal tumors, or from dysentery and water-related ailments. (81)
There, Khavara and Bhānu-gulika are like physicians for poison, yet they are afflicted by poison themselves when Saturn is situated alone in the fifth house from its own Navamśa. 82.
Those born when Ketu alone is present there undoubtedly become experts in the science of archery; when Ketu is alone, one becomes a maker of water-clocks.
In Mercury, the man becomes either a Paramahaṃsa or a staff-bearer (Daṇḍin);
likewise, in Rāhu he is a metal-worker, and in the Sun he becomes a bearer of a sword. (84)
If Mars alone is situated there, the person born will be a bearer of spears and weapons;
or if it is in its own Navamsha, and the Moon and Jupiter are stationed in the fifth house from that same Navamsha, then [the same result follows]. || 85 ||
The author will be born proficient in all branches of knowledge;
however, if Jupiter is there [in the ninth house], he will be an author of works that are somewhat deficient. (86)
If Mercury is there, one is born as an author of even fewer works than that;
if Venus is there, one is born as a poet, eloquent, and a knower of poetry. || 87 ||
One who has untied all knots [of doubt] may live, but not one who is merely eloquent in assemblies and the like;
likewise, one who knows words in particular, as well as one who knows the Vedas and Vedānta.
If Saturn is situated in the aforementioned place, the person will be dull-witted;
if Mercury is situated in the aforementioned place, he will certainly be a Mīmāṃsaka scholar. (89)
If Mars is in its own division or in the fifth house, the person born will be a Naiyāyika philosopher;
and if the Moon is there, he will be a knower of Sāṃkhya and Yoga, a scholar of literature, and a singer. (90)
Under Rāhu, one becomes a knower of Vedānta as well as an expert in song;
under Ketu, one shall be a knower of calculation and proficient in the science of astrology.
The perfect accomplishment of the tradition arises through the connection with a guru;
one should consider it thus, even in the second and third [generations], from one's own portion alone.
Having understood the subtle results in the Bhāva [chart], one should declare the results for the native.
If Ketu is in the second or third house from its own Navāṃśa, the person will be of stammering speech.
O one of evil vision, a man is especially unable to speak [of this] regarding his own [ascendant], the ninth house from the ascendant, or the second and eighth houses. (94)
Kemadruma occurs when there is an equality of malefic planets, especially when they are aspected by the Moon;
and those configurations which have been described by me in this chapter are fruitful [only when not subject to these conditions]. 95.
At the end of the period of the yoga-maker, all [planets] should be known as bestowing their results;
likewise, O twice-born one, by the signs that grant the periods for the second and eighth houses.
When there is an equality of planets [in the ascendant], the inauspicious Kemadruma yoga is to be understood.
At the commencement of a planetary period (daśā), one should calculate the planets along with the ascendant.
In that case as well, this yoga should be understood to occur when there is equality between the significator of wealth (the second house) and the significator of loss (the eighth house).
Thus [is explained] for the houses beginning with the body (the ascendant), for the planets beginning with the Sun, and for the signs beginning with Aries. 98.
The wise man should declare the result according to the specific state [of each planet];
thus, I have briefly described the results of the portions of the *kārakas*. 99.
Now begins the chapter on the yogas that produce results. || 34 ||
O twice-born one, I have thus declared the results according to the portions of the *kāraka*s;
now hear the results of planetary conjunctions based on the lordship of the houses. || 1 ||
Benefic lords of the central houses do not bestow auspicious results;
malefics likewise do not produce inauspicious effects, for the lords of the trines are givers of auspiciousness. (2)

The ascendant (lagna), by virtue of being a quadrant (kendram) or a trine (trikoṇam), is especially conducive to auspiciousness; likewise, the fifth and ninth houses are specifically said to bestow wealth. || 3 ||
The seventh and the tenth houses alone are said to confer special happiness;
all planets that are lords of the third, sixth, and eleventh houses are traditionally considered to yield malefic results. || 4 ||
The lords of the twelfth, second, and eighth houses yield their results through association;
they become increasingly powerful according to the relative strength of their respective positions. (5)
In that regard, because it is the lord of the twelfth house from fortune (the second house), the lord of the eighth house does not bestow auspicious results;
however, if it is the lord of the third, sixth, or eleventh house, or the lord of a *koṇa* (an angle), it yields excellent results.
Among these aforementioned [factors], the stronger configuration (yoga) subverts that which is weak;
here, the defect of being the lord of the eighth house does not apply to the Sun and the Moon. || 7 ||
Jupiter and Venus are declared to be auspicious; the Moon is said to be neutral;
Mercury is known as indifferent; and the Sun, Saturn, and Mars are malefic.
The full moon, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus are strong in ascending order;
the waning moon, the Sun, Saturn, and Mars are also strong in ascending order.
That which is indeed declared as the defect of central lordship applies to the benefics;
however, among the Moon, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus, they are increasingly powerful in successive order.
The lords of the ascendant and the ninth house should be situated in each other's houses, or both should be located in one sign, or at least one of them should be situated in a single sign. (11)
Or, when both gaze at each other with full vision, they then form a union;
through this yoga, one is born as a king or becomes a person of great renown.
When one planet possesses both the lordship of a quadrant and the lordship of a trine, it becomes a particularly significant yoga-producer, whether situated in a quadrant or a trine. || 13 ||

The auspicious influence attributed to malefics by virtue of their lordship over a quadrant does not apply even when they are lords of a trine; it arises solely from being the lord of a quadrant. (14)
When the lords of the tenth and the first houses are themselves the lords of malefic houses, a man does not attain yoga merely through their mutual relationship. || 15 ||
Whether conjoined with the lord of a house or situated in that very house, the two powerful planets Rāhu and Ketu bestow the respective fruits thereof. (16)
If the two dark planets (Rāhu and Ketu) should reside in a quadrant or a trine, being endowed with their own lord or another planet, or being aspected by them, they act as yoga-producers. || 17 ||
O Sage, please tell me: in which ascendant is one born, and which planets act as the formulators of the yoga? Which celestial bodies are the givers of inauspicious results? (18)
O Brahmin, I shall provide the illustration as you have requested:
even if Mars is the lord of the eighth house, it will become well-supported by auspicious planets. (19)
Mars, Mercury, and Venus are malefic; Jupiter and the Sun are benefic.
No auspicious result arises here merely by the conjunction of these planets with the Moon and Jupiter. (20)
Due to the dependence of the living being, even a sinful act is certain;
Śukra would be the direct slayer, characterized as a killer. (21)
Even the planets beginning with Mars would become killers and sinful;
O best of the twice-born, such is the result to be known for one born under the sign of Aries.
Jupiter, Venus, and the Moon are malefic; Saturn and the Sun are benefic.
Saturn brings about royal yoga, while Mercury bestows only slight auspiciousness. (23)
Jīva and the others, as well as Mars, possess the characteristics of being malefics (māraka).
Thus, the results for one born with Taurus as the ascendant should be inferred by the wise. (24)
Mars, Jupiter, and Venus are malefic; Mercury alone is auspicious. The conjunction of Saturn with Jupiter is like the birth of a ram. (25)
This Moon is a destroyer of the face, yet it brings about maturity through its association [with other planets].
Thus, the results arising from the dual signs and the ascendant should be inferred by the wise. (26)
The sons of Bhṛgu and Indu (Mercury and Venus) are malefic; the son of the Earth (Mars), Jupiter, and the Moon are auspicious.
Maṅgala (Mars) himself is the direct fulfiller of complete yoga and the bestower of auspiciousness. || 27 ||
The son of the Sun (Saturn) is the destroyer, while the Sun bestows results through association;
thus have the wise declared the results for one born with Cancer as the ascendant. (28)
Mercury, Venus, and Saturn are malefic planets; Mars, Jupiter, and the Sun bring about auspiciousness.
Auspiciousness arises merely from their conjunction, yet there is no auspiciousness in the conjunction of Jupiter and Venus.
But Saturn, the slayer of Māra, bestows results through association;
the wise man should understand the results for one born in Leo ascendant [as follows]. (30)
Mars, Jupiter, and the Moon are malefic; Mercury and Venus bring auspicious results;
and only Venus and Mercury can become the agents of planetary conjunctions (yogakāraka). || 31 ||
Māra is also a poet, and Sūrya bestows the fruits of association;
thus, the results for one born with Virgo as the ascendant should be inferred by the wise.
The Sun, Mars, and Saturn are malefic planets; Rahu and Mercury are auspicious;
and the Moon and its son (Mercury) become the indicators of a Rajayoga.
Mars destroys [the life-span], while Jupiter and the other malefics possess the characteristics of a "killer" (māraka); Venus is neutral.
Thus are the results to be understood for one born in Libra. (34)
Saturn, Mars, and Rāhu are malefic planets; Jupiter and the Moon are benefic.
Only the Sun and the Moon can become the agents of planetary conjunctions (yogakāraka). || 35 ||
Mars is neutral, while Venus and the others are malefic and possess the characteristics of a killer;
thus should the results for one born under the ascendant of Scorpio be understood. || 36 ||
The planet Mars alone is a wicked poet; both Mars and the Sun are auspicious; the conjunction of the Sun and Mercury is a destroyer; and the son of the Sun (Saturn) is a slayer. (37)
Jupiter is known to yield equal results, while Venus possesses the characteristics of a killer;
thus should the results for one born in Sagittarius ascendant be understood by the wise. (38)
Mars, Jupiter, and the Moon are malefic; Venus and Mercury are benefic.
Saturn himself is not a destroyer; rather, it is the malefics, Mars and the others, who destroy. (39)
The Sun is said to yield equal results, while Venus alone brings about excellent yogas;
thus should the results for one born in the Cancer ascendant be inferred by the wise. (40)
Jupiter, the Moon, and Mars are malefic; Venus and Saturn are benefic. Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus alone bring about royal yoga. (41)
The Sun and Mars are destroyers, while Mercury is said to yield middling results;
thus, the wise should infer the results for one born with Aquarius as the ascendant. 42.
Mars, Venus, the Moon, and Mercury are benefics; the Sun and Saturn are malefics;
Mars and Jupiter are both benefics and yoga-makers; and Mars alone is a yoga-maker. (43)
Even Māra is not his slayer; those two of dull intellect are remembered as the slayers of Māra.
Thus one should contemplate the results for one born with Pisces as the ascendant.
Thus, by the predominance of their dispositions and according to the ascendant at birth, the auspiciousness and inauspiciousness of the planets have been established here. (45)
Furthermore, having reflected upon the yogas of the atmosphere and so forth, the fruit for embodied beings must be declared; and I shall now proclaim them.
Now begins the chapter on celestial configurations (nābhasayoga). || 35 ||
Now, O best of the twice-born, the celestial yogas are being described;
their thirty-two subdivisions amount to one hundred and eighteen.
The three yogas are called the bases (āśraya); then there are two known as petals (dala). Form (ākṛti) is twenty, and the numbers are seven; thus the yogas are proclaimed. || 2 ||
The rope (rajjū), the pestle (musala), and the reed (nala) are the three supports;
those known as the garland (mālā) and the serpent (sarpa) are proclaimed as the two leaf-joins (dalayoga). || 3 ||

The one called the mace (gadā), the one called the cart (śakaṭa), the rhinoceros (sṛṅgāṭaka) and the bird (vihaṃga); likewise the plough (hala), the thunderbolt (vajra), the barley-corn (yava), the lotus (kamala), the water-pot (vāpī), and the sacrificial post (yūpa). || 4 ||
The arrow, the spear, the staff, the boat, the peak, the umbrella, the bow, the half-moon, the discus, and the ocean—these constitute the twenty [mudrās]. || 5 ||
O twice-born one, these seven—saṃkhyā, ākhyā, vallakī, dāma, pāśa, kedāra, and śūlaka—as well as yuga and gola, when joined with the measure of the teeth (danta), are [the names]. 6.

When all [planets] are situated in movable signs, it is known as *rajjū*; when they are situated in fixed signs, it is known as *musala*. When they are situated in dual-natured signs, it is called *nalā*; these are known as the *āśraya* yogas.

When benefic planets occupy the three Kendras, they are known as *dala*, while malefic planets in those positions are known as *mālā* and *bhujaṅga*; these respectively bestow auspicious and inauspicious results. (8)
When all planets occupy both adjacent Kendras, the yoga is called Gadā;
when they occupy the Lagna, the seventh house, and the tenth and fourth houses, it is known as Śakaṭa, and Vihaga.

Yoga is called *Sṛṅgāṭaka* when [the planets] are situated in the ascendant, the fifth house, and the ninth house; another yoga named *Hala* occurs when all [planets] are situated in trines from other houses. (10)

When the benefics are situated in the ascendant and the seventh house, and the malefics are situated in the tenth and fourth houses, the yoga is called Vajra; when they are situated in the reverse order, it is Yava.
When all the planets are mixed and situated in the angles (kendras), it is known as the *kamala* yoga; when all are situated elsewhere than in the angles, the conjunction is called the *vāpī* yoga.
The sacrificial post (yūpa) is formed by four signs from the ascendant; the arrow (śara) by four signs from the fourth house;
the spear (śakti) by four signs from the seventh house; and the staff (daṇḍa) by four signs from the midheaven. || 13 ||

The *kā-kūṭa* is formed by the seventh and ninth signs from the ascendant, and by the seventh signs from the fourth; the *cakra* is likewise from the seventh alone, and the *cāpa* is formed by the seventh signs from the middle sign.
The *cakra* is said to be formed by [planets] situated one sign apart from the ascendant, occupying six houses;
likewise, the *samudra* is formed by those situated one sign apart from the second house, occupying six houses. (15)

When [the planets] are situated in one sign, it is called a *gola*; when situated in two signs, it is named a *yuga*; a *śūla* is said to occur with three divisions, and a *kedāra* with four divisions. (16)
The *pāśa* is formed by [the planets] situated in five signs; that called *dāman* by those occupying six houses;
and *vīṇā* by all [planets] in seven divisions, excluding the others already mentioned. (17)
Men born under the asterism of Rohiṇī are said to always be fond of wandering, handsome, enjoying health in foreign lands, yet cruel and of a wicked nature.
Men born from the Musala yoga are endowed with honor, knowledge, wealth, and other virtues; they are beloved by kings, famous, possessed of many sons, and firm-minded. (19)

Those born under the Nala yoga are characterized by bodies that are either deficient or excessive in size, they possess great accumulations of wealth, are extremely skillful, devoted to their kinsmen, and are handsome in appearance. (20)
Those born under Mālā will be constantly preoccupied with pleasure, endowed with vehicles, clothing, food, and enjoyments; they will be beloved, possess many wives, and be well-born.
Men born from the origin of serpents are wicked, cruel, destitute, constantly afflicted by suffering, and very wretched; they are devoted to consuming and drinking what belongs to others. (22)
In Gadā, however, men are constantly diligent for the sake of wealth, performers of sacrifices, skilled in the sciences and songs, and endowed with riches, gold, and jewels. (23)
Men born under Śakaṭa become afflicted by disease, have deformed nails, are foolish, live by means of carts, are destitute, and are bereft of friends and kinsmen. (24)
Those born under the Vihaga yoga are always fond of wandering, far-famed, live by the service of others, are audacious, and are constantly lovers of quarrels. (25)
Men born at a crossroads are fond of quarreling, lovers of battle, happy, possessed of auspicious wives, wealthy, yet hated by young women. (26)
In the age called Hala, men will always be gluttonous yet impoverished, farmers who are miserable and full of anxiety, abandoned by their kinsmen and friends, and living as servants.
Those born in Vajra are happy in their youth and old age, brave, fortunate, and free from worldly desires; yet they are devoid of luck, wicked, and antagonistic.

Men born in the yoga of Yava are always devoted to vows, restraints, and auspicious rites; being in the middle of their life, they are endowed with happiness, wealth, and sons; they are generous and possess steady minds. (29)

Men born from the lotus-born Brahmā are always characterized by the qualities of liberation: they possess stable lifespans, vast fame, and purity; they perform hundreds of auspicious deeds and rule over the earth. (30)

Those born by the conjunction of Vāpī are kings who possess sharp intellect in the management of treasuries, are endowed with stable wealth and happiness, are blessed with sons, and are greatly delighted by the pleasure of their eyes.
Devoted to the knowledge of the Self and to sacrifice, accompanied by his wife, and endowed with the quality of goodness (sattva),
this man, who delights in vows and observances, was born at the sacrificial post and is most distinguished.
Men are born in Śarayoga as arrow-makers, prison guards, hunters, those devoted to wealth, meat-eaters, violent men, and practitioners of base crafts. (33)
Men born in Śakti are devoid of wealth, fruitless, suffering, base, yet long-lived; they are skilled in the art of war, steadfast, and fortunate.
Men who have lost their children and wives, who are destitute, utterly merciless, and excluded from their own kin;
who are miserable, lowly, and servile, become the source of punishment. (35)
Those who subsist on water, who have great desires, who possess ill-famed reputations, who are wicked, miserly, impure, and greedy—such men born of the sea are indeed base. (36)
Men who dwell in mountain fastnesses are speakers of falsehood, bound by their own sins, destitute, deceitful, cruel, and are always intent on fraud. (37)

One who has the support of kinsmen, is compassionate, beloved by various kings, and possesses excellent intellect, shall be happy and long-lived, bearing the royal parasol during both the first and the last stages of life. (38)
Those born under Kārmukayoga are liars, secret guardians, thieves, gamblers, and addicted to the forest; they are devoid of fortune, yet auspicious in their middle age. (39)
In the yoga known as Ardhacandra, all the generals possess lovely bodies, are dear to the king, are powerful, and are adorned with jewels and gold.
The human being who is born when this yoga occurs becomes a lord of men, his feet shimmering with the radiance of the jewels in the crowns of all the prostrating kings.
Men born from the ocean are enriched with many jewels and wealth, endowed with enjoyments, beloved by their kin and people, possessed of sons, stable in prosperity, and of virtuous character. (42)
Men who are skilled in song, dance, and instrumental music, who are happy and wealthy, who are leaders with many servants—such persons are proclaimed [to be born] under Vīṇā. (43)
One born under Dāman will be a benefactor to virtuous people, endowed with prudence and wealth, renowned as a great lord, enriched with many sons and jewels, steadfast, and wise. (44)
They are subject to bondage by snares, skillful in their undertakings, creators of manifold illusions, talkative, lacking in virtue, possessing many servants, and full of deceit. (45)
Those born in the field (Kedāra) are useful to many, truthful, happy, fickle by nature, and endowed with wealth. (46)
Men born in the Śūla Yoga are sharp-witted yet lazy, devoid of wealth, cruel, utterly outcaste, and great heroes who attain fame in battle. (47)

Those men born during the conjunction of the ages who are proponents of heretical doctrines, devoid of wealth, or outcasts in the world, and who are bereft of the duties toward their sons and mothers; || 48 ||
Men born in the Yoga of Gola become weak, destitute, devoid of learning and wisdom, impure, and perpetually miserable and wretched. (49)
"Your elder brothers declare that it should be understood that these [ten] are fruit-bestowing for all living beings in all ten directions. (50)
Now begins the chapter on various yogas (Atha vividhayogādhyāyaḥ). || 36 ||
If the ascendant is joined with benefics, the yoga is auspicious; if joined with malefics, it is inauspicious.
With benefics or malefics situated in the twelfth house, the yogas are respectively auspicious and inauspicious. (1)
One born from an auspicious conjunction (*śubhayoga*) is eloquent and endowed with beauty, character, and virtues;
one born from a malefic conjunction (*pāpayoga*) is lustful, commits evil deeds, and is intent on the interests of others.

When Jupiter is in the tenth house from the ascendant or from the Moon, conjoined with or aspected by benefics, and free from its sign of debilitation, setting, or the houses of its enemies, this yoga is called Gajakesarī. (3)
A man born under Gajakesarī shall be radiant, wealthy, intelligent, endowed with virtues, and a favorite of the king. || 4 ||

Likewise, when the tenth house from the ascendant as well as from the Moon is joined by exclusively auspicious planets, that yoga is called Amalakīrti; its fame shall endure as long as the moon and stars exist.
Worshipped by kings, possessing great enjoyments, a donor, dear to his kinsmen, a benefactor to others, righteous in soul, rich in virtues, and born of stainless fame. || 6 ||
When the seventh and eighth houses are pure or conjoined with benefic planets, and the quadrants are occupied by benefics, this configuration is known as Parvata.
Fortunate, born in the mountains, eloquent, generous, and learned in the scriptures;
fond of humor, illustrious, radiant, and a leader of cities. || 8 ||

If the lord of the fourth house and Jupiter are mutually situated in quadrant positions while the lord of the ascendant is strong, there is a *kāhala* yoga; or if the lord of the fourth house is in its own exaltation and conjoined with the lord of the tenth house, [there is likewise a *kāhala*].
A man born under Kāhala is vigorous, impetuous, and cunning; endowed with a fourfold army, he becomes a leader of some village or other.
If the lord of the ascendant is in its exaltation, placed in a quadrant, and aspected by Jupiter, one becomes a bearer of the chowrie (a royal attendant).
Alternatively, if two benefics are situated in the ascendant, or in the ninth, tenth, or seventh houses, the same result follows.
Whether a king or a prince, long-lived and wise, eloquent and skilled in all arts, such a person is born in Cāmara. (12)

If the lord of the ascendant is strong and the lords of the fifth and sixth houses are mutually placed in quadrants, or if the lords of the ascendant and the tenth house are in movable signs while the lord of the ninth house is strong; || 13 ||
A man born under the Śaṅkha yoga is endowed with wealth, wife, and sons; he is compassionate, meritorious, highly intelligent, a performer of virtuous deeds, and long-lived. (14)
If the lord of the ninth house is weak, [there is no gain] even if the planets are situated in their own signs, in the twelfth, the first, or the seventh;
however, if the lord of the ninth house is strong, there is gain when it is in a quadrant along with Venus, Jupiter, and the lord of the ascendant. || 15 ||
In the Bherī Yoga, a person becomes a king endowed with wealth, women, and sons, possessed of fame and virtues, well-conducted, happy, and an enjoyer of pleasures. (16)

If the lord of the ascendant is weak, but the planets are situated in a quadrant or a trine in their own or exaltation signs, the Mṛgaṅga yoga is produced; one born under this yoga becomes a king or someone equal to a king, and is happy.

When the lord of the tenth house is in the tenth house in its exaltation, and the lord of the tenth is conjoined with the lord of the ninth, the yoga known as Śrīnātha arises; the king born therein becomes equal to Śukra. || 18 ||
If the lord of the tenth house is in the fifth house or a quadrant, and Mercury and the Sun are strong in their own signs;
and if Jupiter or Mercury is in a trine from the Moon, or Mars is in the eleventh house, there is an autumnal harvest. (19)
In the month of Śarada, a person is born endowed with wealth, wife, and sons; they are happy, learned, dear to kings, ascetic, and devoted to dharma. (20)

When a benefic planet is situated in the ninth house and occupies the fifth house while being joined with both good and evil planets, and a malefic planet is located in the eighth house, this configuration is known as the Matsya (Fish) yoga. || 21 ||
One who knows the proper time, whose form is compassion, and who possesses virtue, intellect, strength, and beauty, as well as fame, learning, and austerity, is indeed born under the Matsya Yoga.
Benefic planets situated in the fifth, sixth, eighth, or fourth houses, or in their own, exaltation, or friendly signs;
and malefic planets situated in the third, eleventh, or ascendant, or in their own or exaltation signs—this is Kūrmayoga. (23)
In the Kūrma-yoga, a person becomes a king—steadfast, endowed with the qualities of righteousness, famous, beneficent, happy, and a leader of men. || 24 ||

When the lord of the ninth house is situated in the second house, the lord of the second house is in the ninth house, and the lord of the ascendant is placed in a quadrant or a trine, that is called Khaḍga Yoga. || 25 ||
One born in the Khaḍga Yoga is endowed with wealth, fortune, and happiness;
he is a knower of the scriptures, rich in intellect and valor, grateful, and skillful. (26)
When the lord of the tenth house is in its own Mūlatrikoṇa or in its own exaltation sign, and the lord of the ascendant is endowed with strength, it is proclaimed as Lakṣmī Yoga. || 27 ||
In the yoga of Lakṣmī, a person becomes handsome, virtuous, a king endowed with many sons and wealth, illustrious, and perfected in dharma. (28)
When the ascendant is fixed, Venus is in a quadrant, the Moon is in a trine and joined by benefics, and Saturn is situated in the tenth house, this yoga is named Kusuma. (29)
In the city called Kusuma, a person is born as a king or one equal to a king, a donor, an enjoyer of pleasures, a happy man, a leader of his clan, virtuous, and learned. (30)
When Jupiter is in the second or fifth house, conjoined with or aspected by Mercury and Venus,
or when those two [Mercury and Venus] have reached the eleventh house, that yoga is known as Kalānidhi.
Born under Kalānidhi, he is virtuous, honored by kings, free from disease, happy, and endowed with wealth and learning. || 32 ||

The lords of the ascendant, the lord of the sign occupied by that [ascendant lord], the lord of the sign occupied by that [lord], and the lord of its Navamsha—if these are situated in a quadrant (kendram), a trine (konam), or in their own exaltation, this configuration is considered the Kalpadruma Yoga. || 33 ||
A man born under Pārijāta becomes a king endowed with all sovereignty, righteous in soul, possessed of strength, fond of battle, and compassionate. (34)

From the lord of the second house, if auspicious planets are situated in the twelfth, eighth, and second houses, it is Hari-yoga; from the lord of the seventh house, if benefics are situated in the fourth, ninth, and eighth houses, it is called Hara-yoga.
If the lords of the fourth, tenth, and eleventh houses from the lord of the ascendant are situated in the ninth house, that yoga is known as Brahma;
one born under this configuration is happy, learned, and endowed with wealth, sons, and other blessings. (36)
When benefic planets occupy the first, fourth, and eighth houses from the ascendant, free from the aspect or conjunction of malefics, it is the Yoga called Lagnādhiyoga;
one born under this yoga is a great soul, learned in the scriptures, and happy.
If the lord of the ascendant is situated in Pārijāta, one is happy; if in Vargottama, one is indeed free from disease.
If situated in Gopura, one is rich in wealth and grain; if situated in Siṃhāsana, one becomes a king. (38)
The wise and illustrious one, together with his vehicle, was born in the world of the gods as Pārāvata;
established upon Airāvata, he became renowned and honored by kings. || 39 ||
Now begins the chapter on the conjunctions of the Moon (Candrayoga). || 37 ||
When the thousand-rayed sun or the moon enters the thorns and so forth in succession,
wealth, intellect, skill, and the like are indeed inferior, middling, or superior.
If the Moon is situated in its own division or in the division of its own great friend during the day and is aspected by Jupiter, one born there will be endowed with wealth and happiness. || 2 ||
If the Moon is situated in its own division or in the division of its own great friend at night, and is aspected by Venus, one born there will be endowed with wealth and happiness. (3)
And when Venus and Jupiter are situated in the opposite of this [the fourth house] and do not aspect it, a child born in this yoga becomes one of little wealth or even destitute. || 4 ||
When benefics are situated in the Moon, the eighth, the tenth, and the first houses, there occurs a *dhiyogaka*;
therein, by the sequence of strength, there shall be a king, a minister, and a commander of the army.
If all the benefic planets have attained an increase from the Moon, the person born will be very wealthy;
if two have increased, he will be moderately wealthy; and with only one, he will be of little means. || 6 ||
Indeed, when a planet is situated in the twelfth, the eleventh, or both houses from the Moon—excluding the Sun—the configurations are respectively named Sunaphā, Anaphā, and Duradhara. (7)
A person who is a king or equal to a king, renowned for his wealth of intelligence, and possessing riches earned by his own arms, is one born from the Sunaphā yoga. || 8 ||
Born under Anaphā, one becomes a king with a healthy body, virtuous, renowned for his fame,
handsome, and endowed with all forms of happiness.
A person born under Duradhara certainly becomes an enjoyer of arisen happiness, a donor endowed with wealth and vehicles, and possesses excellent servants. || 10 ||

If, from the Moon, there is no planet situated in the first, seventh, or twelfth house—unless it be the Sun—or if there is some planet situated in a quadrant from the Ascendant without the Moon; || 11 ||
The yoga known as Kemadruma is highly censured; one born therein is devoid of intellect and learning, and is beset by poverty and calamity. || 12 ||
The Moon yoga specifically destroys the results of other yogas; therefore, the wise person should reflect with diligence that it bestows its own specific fruit. 13.
Now begins the chapter on Raviyoga (the conjunction with the Sun). || 38 ||

From the Sun, with [planets] situated in both [the ninth and fifth houses], excluding the Moon, Mars and the others produce the yogas known as Veśī and Vauśī respectively; likewise, from the Moon, they produce the yoga known as Ubhayacara in sequence. (1)
A mortal born from the conjunction of Veśī is impartial, truthful in speech, tall-bodied, and likewise indolent; though possessing little wealth, he partakes in happiness. || 2 ||
One born in Vośau is skillful, a generous giver, and endowed with fame, knowledge, and strength;
likewise, one born in Ubhayacara becomes a king or someone equal to him, and is happy.
One should contemplate the fruit in this manner when a yoga arises from auspicious planets;
however, when a yoga is produced by malefic planets, the fruit is otherwise.
Now begins the chapter on Rājayoga (39).
Now, therefore, O best of the twice-born, I shall fully explain the methods for acquiring wealth,
by the mere knowledge of which a person becomes honored by kings.
O son of the twice-born, I shall declare before you the essence of those yogas which were formerly proclaimed by Śambhu in the presence of the Daughter of the Mountain.
Or, O twice-born one, one should carefully consider the two planets that clearly produce royal yogas, whether in the Karaka division or in the natal ascendant. (3)
O best of the twice-born, one should likewise establish a single conjunction between the self (the ascendant) and its agent (the Sun), and between the son (the fifth house) and its lord (Venus).

From the relationship between the two—the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the fifth house, who are respectively the self and the son as significators—there arises [the strength] in full, half, or a quarter, according to their respective potencies. (5)
O Brahmin, when the lord of the ascendant is in the fifth house and the lord of the fifth house is in the ascendant,
the significators of children are situated in both the ascendant and the fifth house.

If [the Moon] is in its exaltation, its own Navāṃśa, or its own sign, and is aspected by a benefic planet, the yoga called Mahārāja is produced here; such a person is famous and endowed with happiness. || 7 ||
If the lord of the ninth house is the significator (Kāraka) and is situated in the ascendant, the fifth, or the seventh house,
conjoined with or aspected by benefic planets, it bestows royal yoga.
If the house of wealth, the fourth, or the fifth from both the lord of the ascendant and the significator is occupied by benefic planets, the person born will certainly become a king. || 9 ||

If the third and sixth houses from those two [the Moon and Jupiter] are joined with or aspected by malefic planets, the person born will certainly become a king; if they are mixed, one should declare the results to be mixed.

If Venus is in its own division or in the fifth house, joined with or aspected by Jupiter and the Moon, or if it is in the ascendant or in the lord of the ascendant's sign, the man will belong to the royal class.
If any one of these three—the natal sign, the Kālahorā sign, or the sign of the time of birth—is aspected by a single planet, the person shall attain the status of a king. (12)

O best of the twice-born, when the six divisions of the ascendant (lagna-ṣaḍvarga) are likewise occupied or aspected by a single planet, a royal yoga (rājayoga) certainly occurs; of this there is no doubt.
When the aspect is full, the result is a full conjunction; when the aspect is half, it is exactly half;
and when the aspect is a quarter, it is a quarter-conjunction—thus the results should be understood in sequence. (14)
O twice-born one, if a planet is situated in its own sign or exaltation in three signs from the ascendant, one will certainly become a king;
or else, O twice-born one, if the Drekkāṇa or Navāṃśa in the ascendant is joined by a planet in its exaltation, [the same result follows].

If the fourth house is auspicious and possesses the Moon, and Jupiter likewise occupies the second house, being aspected by a planet situated in its exaltation, there is no doubt that a Rajayoga is formed. || 16 ||
When there is a benefic in the ascendant, a benefic in the second house, a malefic planet in the third house,
and a benefic is situated in the fourth house, one becomes either a king or someone equal to a king.
If the Moon, Jupiter, Venus, or Mercury is situated in its exaltation or placed in the second house, it bestows prosperity upon the embodied soul. (18)
If planets situated in their respective signs of debilitation aspect the ascendant in the sixth, eighth, or third house,
and the lord of the ascendant is placed in its own sign or exaltation, it bestows a yoga for kingship.

If the lords of the sixth, eighth, and twelfth houses are situated in their signs of debilitation, in inimical signs, or in the sixth house, they cause loss; however, if the lord of the ascendant is in its exaltation or own sign and aspects the ascendant, it bestows sovereignty. (20)
The lord of the ninth house, being in its own sign or its exaltation and aspecting the ascendant, bestows kingship;
likewise, benefics situated in the quadrants (kendras) also bestow kingship—of this there is no doubt. (21)
If the Karaka is in a benefic sign and a benefic division, one will be wealthy;
if it is in a benefic [division] within the quadrants (kendras) of that [sign's] division, one certainly becomes a king. || 22 ||

If the sign occupied by the lord of the ascendant and the sign occupied by the lord of the seventh house are mutually situated in a quadrant, or in the third or eleventh house, or in a trine, then one becomes a king; of this there is no doubt. (23)
One observes the ascendants known as the Bhāva-horā and Ghaṭī;
furthermore, there is a Rājayoga when two planets are in their exaltations, or even when there are two ascendants. (24)
Whether from the sign and decanate, or from the sign and degree, or even from the sign and decanate, the lord of the ascendant bestows yoga when it aspects [the relevant house]. (25)
When a sign is occupied by a planet in its own exaltation, especially by the Moon, or occupied by Jupiter and Venus, or by any other planet in its exaltation; || 26 ||
In the absence of malefic obstructions, there is no doubt that a Rājayoga is formed;
likewise, when the Moon is in an auspicious *ārūḍha* and Jupiter is in the second house.
O best of the twice-born, it should be known that even if the lord of the eighth house is situated in its sign of debilitation, if it aspects the ascendant, a royal yoga (rājayoga) still occurs. (28)
If the fourth or tenth house is aspected by its lord from the ascendant, and Venus aspects the eleventh house from the ascendant while the ārūḍha lagna is auspicious; || 29 ||
A king or someone equal to him will certainly be born, provided that [the Moon] is situated in the sixth or eighth house, is debilitated, or likewise aspects the ascendant. (30)
If the lord of the third house is in its sign of debilitation and aspects the ascendant, or likewise [if it is so placed],
and there is a benefic in a quadrant from the navāṃśa of the ascendant, one is capable of both restraint and favor.
Now I shall fully explain the supreme Rājayoga and others,
along with the results arising from the specific positions of the planets and the influence of their aspects and yogas.
If the lord of the house of asceticism (the ninth) and the minister (the fifth), especially as the lord of the mantra-house (the fifth),
are both mutually aspecting each other when born, one becomes a possessor of sovereignty in this world.
Wherever those two, even if joined with others, form a Sama-saptama yoga, a child born in a royal lineage will certainly become a king. (34)

Likewise, if the lord of the vehicle is in the house of measurement and the lord of measurement is situated in the house of the vehicle, and he is seen by the lords of the Buddha and the Dharma, then one possesses sovereignty in this world. (35)
He whose birth [chart] has the lords of the fourth, tenth, eleventh, and first houses conjoined with Jupiter is a king, renowned for his fame throughout the ends of the earth. (36)
If he is born here conjoined with Sukhakarmādipa or with Mantrinātha, or joined with Dharmanātha, he shall possess royal power.

If the lord of the fifth house is joined with the lord of the ninth house or the lord of the ascendant, and is situated in the ascendant, the fourth house, or the tenth house, the person born shall become a king. (38)
If Jupiter is situated in the ninth house (dharmasthāna), conjoined with Venus in its own house,
or joined with the lord of the fifth house, one born under such conditions becomes a possessor of royal power in this world.
From the midpoint of the day and from the midpoint of the night, the auspicious time (velā) lasts for two and a half nāḍikās;
one born during that time shall become a king or equal to one.
The Moon looks at the Sage (Venus), and the Sage looks at the Moon; when they thus gaze at one another while situated in the three worlds, it is in some cases declared to be a Rājayoga. (41)
If the Moon is situated in its Vargottama division, is strong, and is aspected by four or more planets, the person born will certainly become a king. (42)
Even one born when the ascendant has reached its highest degree (uttamāṃśa), provided it is aspected by four or more planets other than the Moon, shall become a lord of the earth.
If the planets are situated in their exaltations even in small numbers, there will be a king born of a royal lineage;
otherwise, one born of another family will be equal to a king and endowed with wealth. || 44 ||
Even one born of a low lineage certainly becomes a king if there are four or five planets situated in their exaltations or their triplicities. (45)
With six planets situated in their exaltations, one attains the status of a universal monarch (cakravartin).
O best of the twice-born, in this manner, various types of royal yogas are to be understood.
If the single planet Jupiter, or Venus, or Mercury is situated in its exaltation sign and joined by a benefic planet in a quadrant, one shall become a king or equal to a king. (47)
If all the benefic planets are situated in the Kendras and all the malefic planets are in the third, sixth, and eleventh houses, even one born of a low lineage will certainly become a king. (48)
Now begins the chapter on the yoga of royal connections (Chapter 40).
If the lord of the tenth house from the birth ascendant is conjoined with or aspected by the lord of the ninth house,
or even by the significator of ministers, one attains a position of prominence in the royal court.
O Brahmin, when the eleventh house is aspected by the lord of the eleventh and is free from the influence or aspect of malefic planets, then one attains preeminence in the royal palace.
Even when conjoined with Kārakendra as the minister-kāraka, a child endowed with sharp intellect will certainly become a royal minister. (3)
If the lord of the ninth house is strong, conjoined with benefics, and situated in its own sign or its exaltation, one will certainly become a royal minister. ||4||
If Amātyakāraka is in the ascendant, or in the fifth or ninth house, the child will become a royal minister and famous; of this there is no doubt. || 5 ||
If the lord of the Atmakaraka is in a quadrant or a trine from the Amatyakaraka,
then the person born is endowed with royal favor, dependent upon a king, and happy.
O best of the twice-born, when malefic planets are in the third and sixth houses from both the ascendant and from such a [strong] Karaka, one is born as a commander of an army.
If a planet is situated in a quadrant, a trine, its exaltation, or its own sign, and is conjoined with or aspected by the lord of the ninth house, one will certainly become a royal minister. || 8 ||
If the lord of the birth sign is in the ascendant and conjoined with a benefic, this is the primary yoga for becoming a minister; there is no doubt that it will occur in old age.
If a benefic planet is conjoined with the lord of the ascendant in the fifth, the seventh,
the tenth, or the ninth house, wealth shall arise from royal patronage.
O best of the twice-born, if the ninth house is in the ascendant, or if the significator is in the ninth house, this is undoubtedly an indication of a connection with royalty.
If the lord of the eleventh house is situated in the eleventh house, free from the aspect of malefic planets,
and the Karaka (significator) is conjoined with benefics, he shall obtain gain from the king's palace.

When the lord of the ascendant is situated in the tenth house and the lord of the tenth house is situated in the ascendant, this is proclaimed as a powerful yoga for association with royalty. || 13 ||
O best of the twice-born, when Venus and the Moon occupy the fourth house from the Karaka in one's birth chart,
that person is born endowed with the insignia of royalty.
If the lord of the ascendant or the significator (Kāraka) is conjoined with the lord of the fifth house and situated in a quadrant or a trine, that man will become a friend of the king. || 15 ||
